Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and σφάλλω (to "fail"); secure (literally or figuratively):--certain(-ty), safe, sure.
BiblicalUsage: This is the word for what cannot slip or fail. The hope set before us is an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, Paul says writing the same things again is safe for his readers, and the chief captain wanted to know the certainty of the charges against Paul.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the anchor holds because of where it is fastened, inside the veil where Christ has gone before us. That is the whole ground of our safety, and I hold it fast when everything else feels like it is giving way.
